title: Certified Verification of Input-Oblivious Unambiguous Hierarchies
abstract: Edward A. Hirsch (arXiv:2611.33126, Nov 2026) analyzed input-oblivious unambiguous complexity hierarchies built from OUP, proving that OUH <= P^{TALLY cap NP} <= P^{ONP}_|| (Thm. 4.1), the loose promise-oracle hierarchy satisfies OUH^bullet <= OGTD[NP] = OUGTD[FP^{ONP}, co-ONP, P] = P/OptP <= OUM cap P^{ONP} (Lem. 3.1, Thm. 5.1), the alternating oblivious unambiguous dot-operator hierarchy collapses to OUP cup co-OUP at level 2 (Thm. 6.2, Cor. 6.3), single loose promise queries reduce to language queries (Thm. 6.5), and SOUP = OUP cap co-OUP (Prop. 6.6). We construct a standalone zero-dependency Lean 4.35.0 formalization of 18 core lexicographic-advice, Mahaney-census, Cantor-pairing, loose-tower descent, dot-operator collapse, guardedness, and SOUP theorems (zero sorry, zero warnings, zero Classical.choice) paired with an exact discrete four-mode certificate verifier (OUH-CERT-1.0). Across 16 canonical certificates (0.033-0.210 ms, total 1.64 ms), all invariants replay identically while rejecting 60/60 live adversarial forgery attacks.
